attributes.affiliation_basis: UNKNOWN: ADS-B states an identity and nothing in it is authenticated, so nothing here infers a side
attributes.entity_id_basis: the trace's address under ADSB_NONICAO, upper-cased as the adsb adapter writes it, so a frame and a trace of one airframe give one entity_id
attributes.entity_type_basis: PLATFORM: a trace is one airframe's history. The emitter category in an aircraft object is sampled on some points only and is not read as a type
attributes.kinematics_basis: the last point: element 4 (ground speed, knots), element 5 as course only when the point is airborne (on the ground it is the true heading and stays in the residual; 360 is not a course this field holds), element 7 (vertical rate, feet per minute, barometric by flag bit 2); a null element is an unknown, never zero
attributes.position_basis: the trace's last point, the Track's last sample
attributes.position_source_basis: element 9 is adsb_other: the aircraft's own position report, received over ADS-B or rebroadcast over ADS-R, so the fix is its own navigation solution
attributes.quality_basis: the last point: source_quality is element 9, the source readsb names; rc_m is the radius of containment in metres from element 8's aircraft object, an integrity bound and not a one-sigma accuracy, so accuracy_m is never set; a point without either states nothing here
attributes.readsb_samples_basis: readings taken from each point, keyed by sample index: index i is Track.samples[i] and residual.data.trace[i]. on_ground is element 3 being ground; element_5 says whether element 5 is a track or, on the ground, a true heading; the four booleans are element 6's bits 0 to 3; elements is how many elements the point states
attributes.symbol_basis: derived from affiliation; a trace states no symbol
attributes.valid_from_basis: the instant of the trace's first point
attributes.valid_to_basis: the instant of the trace's last point: the file holds nothing after it, which says nothing about the airframe after it
attributes.vertical_basis: element 3, barometric altitude in feet (flag bit 3 clear), as stated; alt_m is metres above the ellipsoid and a pressure altitude is not one

transformations: icao: the address is upper-cased for its source id, as the adsb adapter writes it, so one airframe has one entity_id across both adapters
trace[*][0]: a point's instant is timestamp + element 0, summed in decimal from the shortest text of each number, then rendered to the CDM's millisecond form
trace[-1][4]: the last point's ground speed in knots becomes metres per second (x 1852/3600)
trace[-1][7]: the last point's vertical rate in feet per minute becomes metres per second (x 0.00508)

completeness.completeness_basis: carried_samples counts the trace's points; readsb writes one permanent trace per airframe per UTC day, so a file is a window of the airframe's history and never the whole of it; the trace states no total

payload.event_id_basis: the address and the trace's first and last instants
payload.event_type_basis: TRACK_UPDATE: one trace file is one update of one airframe's history
payload.observed_at_basis: the instant of the trace's last point: timestamp + element 0, on the aggregator's clock (readsb stamps a point with the system time at which the message reached it); the aircraft states no time
payload.received_at_basis: the injected clock; a trace states no delivery instant
payload.severity_basis: INFO: a trace states no urgency; an emergency code in an aircraft object stays in the residual
payload.validity_basis: no validity: the event is an instant, and the span the trace covers is the Entity's valid_from and valid_to and the Track's samples
